meta.title: WaterUI — Cross-platform UI for Rust
meta.description: Write once, apply everywhere. WaterUI is a cross-platform UI framework for Rust that renders through UIKit, AppKit, Android Views, GTK4, the GPU, or an ESP32.

hero.lead: WaterUI maps each view onto the platform's own toolkit: UIKit, AppKit, Android Views, GTK4. Where none fits, it draws the view itself, on the GPU or on a microcontroller.
hero.status: Pre-1.0 · Apple and Android are the most complete backends

bond.caption: A value changes, its readers update. Nothing else is touched.

targets.title: Targets
targets.lead: One view tree, five backends. Each one speaks the platform's own toolkit, or draws the view itself when there is none.
targets.dewNote: The same view that becomes a UIKit control on an iPhone runs on a microcontroller with no OS and no GPU.

reactivity.title: State
reactivity.lead: State is plain values. There is no virtual tree to diff, and changing one string never rebuilds the subtree around it.

binding.title: Binding<T> is mutable state
binding.body: Put a value in a Binding and hand it to views. Any view that reads it updates when it changes.

computed.title: Computed<T> is derived state
computed.body: Map a Binding into a Computed. Signal-aware APIs accept either, and only their readers update.

collections.title: Collections diff by identity
collections.body: Give List or ForEach a reactive collection of Identifiable items and membership changes are diffed by id.

features.title: Batteries
features.lead: Layouts, controls, forms, navigation, media, charts, and the platform services around them. One dependency.

controls.title: Controls and forms
items: Buttons, text fields, sliders, steppers, toggles
#[form] derives a whole form from a struct
Lists and ForEach diffed by id

navigation.title: Navigation and windows
items: Typed navigation paths, persisted with serde
Multiple windows with their own styles
Locale and layout direction from the environment

graphics.title: Graphics and motion
items: GPU image filters and shader surfaces
Animation on a deterministic frame clock
Gestures, hover, cursor, drag and drop

media.title: Media and data
items: Barcodes and web views: WebKit, CEF, WPE, Chromium

icons.title: Icons
items: Native icon per platform, one API

kit.title: WaterKit
kit.lead: The platform services around the UI: one Rust API per capability, a native implementation on each platform.

testing.title: Testing
testing.lead: Accessibility-first tests run under plain cargo test against the Hydrolysis renderer. No simulator, no device. Interactions are assertions, and every wait pumps to quiescence instead of sleeping.

previews.title: Previews
previews.lead: Any function marked #[preview] renders to an image without launching the app. The same surface drives semantic interaction tests and GPU measurements.

commands.render: Render a view to a PNG

previews.imageCaption: Output of water preview on the {{example}} example.
previews.dogfood: Every screenshot on this page was produced this way.

quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.lead: A playground is a plain Rust crate. The CLI keeps native projects out of your source tree and manages them on demand.
quickStart.entryPoint: That is the whole entry point. The app crate depends on waterui and nothing else.

tools.doctor: reports what a toolchain is missing

quickStart.shipping: Ready to ship? App mode generates platform projects that belong to you, so they can be customized, signed, and packaged.

gallery.lead: Runnable applications from the repository, rendered by the framework's own preview command.
